clue.text: Delightful stupor with music playing

indicators.note: music playing suggests the letters being performed in a new arrangement, so they are shuffled

explanation.surface: A dazed listener finds a torpor brought on by music rather lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' signals that the letters of STUPOR and MUSIC are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something extremely enjoyable, usually food, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Wreck meal to welcome Conservative

indicators.note: welcoming a guest means taking them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A Tory guest ruins dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink a ship deliberately, hence to ruin or wreck a plan.

clue.text: Haggard equestrian?

parts.note: His middle name also means a horseman

explanation.surface: A worn-out horseman looks gaunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' looks like an adjective meaning gaunt; it is the novelist H. Rider Haggard.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on horseback, and also the Victorian novelist's middle name.

clue.text: Drink a small measure served up by woman

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a gram is a small unit of weight
Rita is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman pours out a little tot of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail of tequila and lime juice, a definition by example.

clue.text: Warm cloth: awesome clothes

indicators.note: clothes as a verb means covers, so the answer is held within the words

explanation.surface: A wonderful garment keeps a wearer cosy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb: the phrase 'cloth awesome' wraps the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To melt or become less cold, a synonym of warming up.

clue.text: Hard-hearted former pupil of the French judge

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil of a school
du is French for of the
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: An old boy of a French school is an unfeeling judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubbornly unmoved and unrepentant, a synonym of hard-hearted.

clue.text: Mostly remain in disgrace

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: to stay is to remain

explanation.surface: Someone lingers, largely, under a cloud of shame.
explanation.definitionFit: A blot on one's reputation is a mark of shame or dishonour.

clue.text: Increase in post regularly received by upmarket press

indicators.note: what is received is taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: U means upper class, as in U and non-U
to urge is to press

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: More mail is arriving at a posh newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes P and S from POST; 'received by' sets them between U and URGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden rise or surge is an increase.

clue.text: Cold friend only in underwear

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
ami is French for friend
sole means only, as in sole survivor

explanation.surface: A chilly companion has nothing on but their undies.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's light sleeveless undergarment for the upper body, an example of lingerie.

clue.text: Sneaky sort of service

definitions.meaning: a serve in tennis or similar games delivered with the hand below the shoulder

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both deceitful conduct and a delivery of the ball made with the arm kept low.

clue.text: Get together when entertaining graduates

indicators.note: a host entertaining guests holds them within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
MAs are holders of a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Students meet up at a moment when graduates are being hosted.
explanation.definitionFit: To collect or accumulate is a synonym of gathering things together.

clue.text: Hard-up criminal in seclusion

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A penniless crook lies low in hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the practice in some Muslim and Hindu communities of keeping women hidden, hence any state of seclusion.

clue.text: Losing heart, forty-niner dynamited to get edge

indicators.note: blown apart by explosive, so the remaining letters are scattered and rearranged
the heart of a word is its middle, here the two central letters, which are dropped

explanation.surface: A gold-rush prospector, dispirited, blasts his way to the boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing heart' drops YN from the middle of FORTYNINER, leaving FORTINER; 'dynamited' rearranges that. A forty-niner was a prospector in the 1849 California gold rush.
explanation.definitionFit: A border or limit of settled territory, the outer edge of a country.

clue.text: Reportedly smell lubricant and shy away

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard or said, so the words are spoken aloud

parts.note: reek means smell and oil is a lubricant; said together they make the sound

explanation.surface: Someone flinches at the stink of engine grease.
explanation.definitionFit: To flinch or draw back in fear or disgust is a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Disdain shown by new office worker in bed

indicators.note: in puts the new office worker inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
a temp is a temporary office worker

explanation.surface: Scorn greets a new temp who turns up in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorn and disdain are synonyms for looking down on someone.

clue.text: Hold up single actor

parts.note: to stall is to delay or hold up
single means one

explanation.surface: A lone performer is held up on set.
explanation.definitionFit: Sylvester Stallone is an American film actor, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Canals spoiled their oddly northern city

indicators.note: spoiled suggests damaged, so the letters are rearranged
oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of the word

explanation.surface: Waterways in some northern town have been ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoiled' rearranges CANALS into LANCAS; 'oddly' takes T, E and R from THEIR.
explanation.definitionFit: The county town of Lancashire in north-west England, a definition by example.

clue.text: Spreadsheet program, according to Sean Connery, that's easily cracked

indicators.note: the Scottish actor famously pronounced an S as SH, so the word is said aloud in his voice

parts.note: Excel is Microsoft's spreadsheet software

explanation.surface: Bond's actor mispronounces the name of office software.
explanation.walkthrough: Connery's slurred SH turns 'Excel' into 'Ekshell', near enough to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin shell of an egg breaks very easily, so it is the thing that is fragile.

clue.text: Dance enthusiast, about to be replaced by daughter, is able to perform

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast

indicators.note: one letter is swapped out and another put in its place

parts.note: can means is able
C stands for circa, Latin for about
go can mean to work or function, as a machine performs

explanation.walkthrough: In CAN, 'about' (C) is replaced by 'daughter' (D), giving DAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Spanish dance in triple time, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Sweet and loving worker

parts.note: fond means affectionate or loving
the worker ant is a crossword favourite for worker

explanation.surface: A kind and affectionate employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like an adjective alongside 'loving'; it is a noun, the confection.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft sugar paste used for icing and confectionery, an example of a sweet.

clue.text: Remove from place on security council?

definitions.meaning: to remove from a seat or position, especially a horse rider or office holder
read as two words, a seat at the United Nations, home of the Security Council

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to dislodge from office, and split in two it names a seat at the United Nations.

clue.text: Hair covering hide of imposing beast

indicators.note: covering means wrapped round, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

indicators.note: a hide is an outer skin, so only the outside letters of the word are kept

explanation.definitionFit: A female tiger is an example of a wild animal.

clue.text: Unnecessary bait in front of ship

clue.text: Taking top off, behave badly in store

parts.note: to play up is to misbehave

explanation.surface: A shopper strips off and causes a scene in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: To put aside or stockpile for later use is to store.

clue.text: Nail chorus heard to be tricky

indicators.note: heard means listened to, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: a tack is a small nail, and to chorus is to sing together

explanation.surface: A choir singing about nails proves a difficult piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Something demanding or burdensome is hard work, a synonym of difficult.

clue.text: Detective visiting TT venue, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: a visitor goes into a place, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Isle of Man (IOM) hosts the TT motorcycle races
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A police officer attends the motorbike races, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: An expression or turn of phrase is a way of saying things.

clue.text: Drive second, going over flag

parts.note: on a golf green the flagstick is called the pin

clue.text: Fruity request?

definitions.meaning: having the taste of a common orchard fruit, an invented adjective
to make a formal request, as for a job

explanation.definitionFit: Read as an adjective it means like the orchard fruit; as a verb it means to ask formally.

clue.text: Understand European politician is overcome by terrible heat

terrible suggests something ruined, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Continental member of parliament wilts in a dreadful heatwave.

clue.text: Abba solos wow Anna?

parts.note: each of the four words reads the same forwards and backwards, so they are examples of such words

explanation.surface: A pop fan asks whether the Swedish band's solo numbers dazzled someone named Anna.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: ABBA, SOLOS, WOW and ANNA are all symmetrical words.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that read identically in either direction; every word of the clue is one.
